note: Reference photos of the place. Open one for the angle, the light, and how to take it.

shots.angle: From the bottom of the steps, camera at your eyes, the hall centered. Leave the incense burner in the foreground if it is there.
shots.light: The hall faces south. Morning sun hits the front. Midday the porch is dark. Expose for the wood, not the sky.
how: Stand off the center line so you are not in the worshippers' path.
No pose in the doorway. A person on the steps, small, back to you, is enough.
Take it, then one frame of a single lantern under the eaves.

shots.angle: From the west side of the courtyard, camera at your eyes, pagoda against the sky. Step back until all five roofs fit.
shots.light: Sun on one side of the red wood, shade on the other. A flat grey sky still works if the pagoda is the only thing in the frame.
how: Keep people at the bottom edge, or leave them out.
Hold the camera straight so the pagoda does not lean.
Take one wide and one of a single roof corner.

shots.angle: Kneel and point up. The roofs stack. Cut off the base if you have to.
shots.light: Sun on one side of the red wood, shade on the other. A flat grey sky still works if the pagoda is the only thing in the frame.
how: Hold the camera straight so the pagoda does not lean.
Take one wide and one of a single roof corner.

shots.angle: Close, camera a hand's width from the paper knots. The rack fills the frame.
shots.light: Shade. The papers are white. If they burn out, turn so the sun is not on them.
how: Your hands can be in the frame, tying one paper. Do not photograph a stranger's hands up close.
Focus on the nearest knot.
Take two. One with your hands, one of the papers only.

shots.angle: Stand on the east or west side of the gate and shoot through the opening, so the lantern is a circle and the street is a tunnel.
shots.light: Side light. One edge of the gate bright, the inside of the tunnel darker.
how: A person walks through the opening, small.
Keep the camera level.
Wait until the opening is not full of faces.

shots.angle: Same side, lower. Put the lantern in the top corner and the stone floor in the bottom.
shots.light: Side light. One edge of the gate bright, the inside of the tunnel darker.
how: Keep the camera level.
Wait until the opening is not full of faces.

shots.angle: Hold the camera lower, near your waist, and point up a little. Same place, more sky or more ceiling.
shots.light: Morning is the useful light. The gate is in sun, and the street is not packed yet. After 10:00, wait for a gap.
how: You are in front of the temple, on the shopping street that leads to it.
Match the reference, then take one step left or right so a stranger is not in the middle.
Take two frames. Keep the sharper one.
If a person is in it, they are your group, looking at the place, not at the lens.

shots.angle: Stand in the middle of the street, camera at your eyes, the kappa figure centered above the shops.
shots.light: Daylight on the sign. If the sign is in shade and the sky is white, come back when the sun is on it, or point up and leave the sky out.
how: Nobody needs to pose. If a person walks under the sign, let them be small.
Hold the camera straight.
Take one with the street empty enough to read the sign.

shots.look: Kappa sign over the street, closer
shots.angle: Closer, pointed up, so the kappa fills the top and the shop signs stack under it.
shots.light: Daylight on the sign. If the sign is in shade and the sky is white, come back when the sun is on it, or point up and leave the sky out.
how: Hold the camera straight.
Take one with the street empty enough to read the sign.

shots.angle: From one end of a block, camera at your chest, the street and the signs going away from you.
shots.light: Even daylight. Signs in the shade are better than a blown sky.
how: Walk while you shoot, camera at your chest, so you are not standing in the road.
Take one frame per block, not ten of the same view.
Step to the curb if a truck comes.
